elements.element: Renewal must not occur at Vendor's unilateral option and must instead either require mutual written agreement or operate automatically.
elements.evidence: Article IV.I permits renewal only “by mutual written agreement of the parties,” and Article IV.III likewise requires mutual written agreement for additional extensions.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, each renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: The automatic-renewal condition is demonstrably absent because renewal requires mutual written agreement. The clause nevertheless specifies successive 12-month renewal periods.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Customer must be able to opt out on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The automatic-renewal condition is demonstrably absent because renewal requires mutual written agreement, so no opt-out mechanism is needed under the selected mutual-agreement structure.

elements.element: If automatic renewal is used, Vendor must provide a reminder 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: The automatic-renewal condition is demonstrably absent because renewal requires mutual written agreement, so the reminder requirement is inapplicable under the selected structure.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no renewal price-increase cap or CPI limitation.
The rendered clause requires mutual written agreement for renewal and therefore does not provide automatic renewal.

elements.element: Customer must have a non-renewal right exercisable with a notice window of no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no automatic-renewal mechanism, non-renewal right, or notice window.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at 5%.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no 5% price-increase cap.

result.reason: The redline appropriately eliminates Vendor's unilateral seven-year renewal option and replaces it with mutual written agreement for successive 12-month periods. However, it omits the required renewal price cap, so it does not satisfy the preferred position. It also does not satisfy the separately assessed fallback because renewal is not automatic and there is no non-renewal window or 5% cap. The drafting retains redundant renewal provisions and the malformed phrase “mutual written of the parties,” but it leaves unrelated termination terms intact and introduces no clear contradiction.
